subject: Some Observations on multipleGroup output in vertical equating

messages.author: 08b39a7ab9f8d02c
messages.subject: Some Observations on multipleGroup output in vertical equating
parts: Hi All: When one has multiple groups with some overlapping items as in 2 stage testing or irt vertical equating, the command 'coef(result,IRTpars=TRUE,simplify=TRUE) does not give one the traditional IRT parameters and you have to rescale the 'a' parameter by dividing by 1.7. When subjects take 20 or more items in the two stage testing situation (vertical equating), the default extimation procedures yield results that nicely replicate those of commercial software such as bilog-mg with the above rescaling.  In the neighborhood of 15 items, default estimation is quite a bit off from bilog-mg, but if one does MHRM the estimates  become much closer.  This is not surprising since bilog-mg uses EM followed by Newon-Raphson. In a 9 item example with 3 unique items in each of two groups and thus 3 common items, multipleGroup yields some "off-the wall" estimates while bilog-mg yields seemingly reasonable estimates for this admittedly minimum information example.  Now bilog-mg does have default priors but it is hard to replicate them in the multipleGroup except possibly for the 'a' parameter. One other observation, command 'summary' does not seem to work for MHRM estimation. All of these examples are one dimensional dichotomous items.Cheers Don Rock

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Some Observations on multipleGroup output in vertical equating
parts:
Hi Don,

Sounds like some interesting observations, some of which sound a little peculiar since I wouldn't expect bilog to provide results that are so discrepant (I have used multipleGroup pretty extensively, and it provides results that I would expect). Could you provide something that I could reproduce to see these issues, perhaps generated with the simdata() function and analysed with bilog/mirt to obtain the suitable text output files? Cheers.

Phil
